paragraphs: A forecasting model can give different predictions for the same future timestamp when its input window shifts. That creates a reliability problem beyond ordinary prediction error: successive forecasts may fluctuate even when they refer to the same target. This paper studies that inconsistency in models that predict long sequences of future values from recent observations.

AliO addresses the problem by reducing differences between predictions for shared timestamps across shifted input sequences. It encourages agreement in both the time domain and the frequency domain, addressing alignment through two representations of the forecasts. The paper also introduces the Time Alignment Metric, or TAM, to measure agreement between predictions. This captures a property that mean squared error against observed values does not directly measure.

The experiments report alignment improvements of up to 58.2% in TAM while maintaining or improving forecasting performance, with improvements in forecasting performance reaching 27.5%. These are reported maxima. The findings support evaluating forecast consistency alongside accuracy when assessing long-term forecasting reliability.
neurips-2025-alio-output-alignment-matte.tldr: AliO makes forecasts for the same timestamp more consistent across shifted input windows while maintaining or improving prediction performance.

paragraphs: Manufacturers collaborating through Bayesian networks may need joint predictions while keeping their model structures and parameters confidential. Existing confidential inference methods described here support discrete variables, whereas practical settings also involve continuous measurements. Hybrid CCJT extends collaborative inference to this mixed setting without requiring continuous variables to be discretized.

The framework first constructs a strongly rooted junction tree across the participating parties. Interface cliques provide the connections needed to organize their separate models into this shared inference structure. A protocol based on multiparty computation then combines a one-time alignment phase with belief propagation across the tree. Its confidentiality setting assumes semi-honest participants who do not collude, so that assumption is part of the framework's scope.

Across nine datasets, the authors report an average 32% improvement in predictive accuracy for continuous targets over the compared state of the art. In purely discrete settings, communication costs fall by a median factor of 10.4. These results address two distinct benefits: supporting continuous predictions more accurately and reducing communication for discrete inference.
neurips-2025-collaborative-and-confident.tldr: Hybrid CCJT enables confidential collaborative inference with discrete and continuous variables under semi-honest, non-colluding participants.

paragraphs: Robot policies need to generate actions that depend on their inputs, including visual and language information. This paper identifies a training failure in conditional diffusion policies: when conditions are difficult to distinguish, the objective can degenerate into learning the overall action distribution. The authors call this loss collapse because the training objective loses the intended dependence on the condition.

Cocos changes the source distribution used in conditional flow matching so that it depends on the condition. It anchors that distribution around semantic information extracted from the inputs. This builds condition information into the starting distribution of the generation process, encouraging the policy to integrate it more strongly and preventing the identified collapse.

The paper provides theoretical justification and experiments in simulation and real-world settings. It reports faster convergence and higher success rates than existing approaches, including matching large pretrained vision-language-action models with substantially fewer gradient steps and parameters. The method is presented as lightweight and compatible with multiple policy architectures, making the training change broadly reusable.
neurips-2025-conditioning-matters-traini.tldr: Cocos improves diffusion-policy training by making the source distribution condition-dependent, preventing an identified loss-collapse failure.

paragraphs: In a networked bandit problem, an action at one node can change rewards at other nodes. Learning which actions work therefore involves interconnected outcomes. A further tension arises when a learner repeatedly chooses its currently preferred action: doing so can reduce regret while leaving too little information to estimate the performance of less frequently selected actions accurately.

This paper formalizes that tension for adversarial, design-based bandits with network interference. Its main theoretical contribution is a Pareto frontier between regret and inference accuracy. Such a frontier characterizes the trade-off between the two objectives, clarifying why a method optimized for reward collection alone may be unsuitable when reliable statistical estimates are also required.

The authors also introduce an anytime-valid asymptotic confidence sequence and the EXP3-N-CS algorithm to balance these objectives. The confidence-sequence contribution concerns uncertainty assessment across time, with an explicitly asymptotic qualification. Together, the results make statistical inference part of the bandit design problem alongside sequential reward optimization.
neurips-2025-design-based-bandits-under-.tldr: The paper characterizes the regret–inference trade-off in networked bandits and proposes an algorithm with an anytime-valid asymptotic confidence sequence.

paragraphs: Mixed-precision quantization assigns different numerical bit widths to different network layers, reducing memory and inference costs while allocating precision where it matters. Choosing those assignments efficiently is difficult, especially if the resulting policy should transfer across datasets. GMPQ-TE addresses both goals using topological entropy as a measure of each layer's sensitivity to quantization.

The method computes this measure from minibatches whose examples share a label. The authors observe that topological entropy is consistent across datasets and strongly associated with both quantized accuracy and bit width. Those observations motivate formulating precision allocation as a single-pass linear programming problem, avoiding a lengthy policy search. The reported policy-generation time for MobileNet-V2 is 11 seconds.

Experiments show that a policy obtained using CIFAR-10 can transfer to ImageNet and PASCAL VOC. The method also achieves a competitive balance between accuracy and computational complexity against existing mixed-precision approaches. The findings support the usefulness of this sensitivity measure for fast, transferable precision allocation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-efficient-and-generalizable.tldr: GMPQ-TE uses topological entropy to allocate layer precision quickly and produces quantization policies that transfer across the evaluated datasets.

paragraphs: An agent pursuing a utility function may change its behavior when running out of resources can terminate its action sequence. The possibility of termination introduces implicit trade-offs into otherwise rational decision-making. This paper studies how such pressure can shift an agent's preferences toward or away from risk, even when it is acting on behalf of a human.

The authors formalize the problem using a survival bandit framework. Their analysis focuses on how constraints affect sequential choices and how differences between the human's and agent's exposure to those constraints can create misalignment. The central issue is that pursuing utility under survival pressure can produce incentives that differ from the objectives of the person commissioning the agent.

The paper provides theoretical and empirical results quantifying these preference shifts, identifies conditions under which misalignment emerges, and proposes mechanisms to mitigate risk-seeking or risk-averse behavior. Its contribution is a framework for interpreting constraint-driven behavior and informing deployment in resource-limited environments. The stated results concern conditions for these effects, rather than asserting that all constrained agents become misaligned.
neurips-2025-emergent-risk-awareness-in-.tldr: A survival bandit framework explains how resource constraints can shift rational agents' risk preferences and create conditional misalignment with human objectives.

paragraphs: An image can look convincing while failing to follow a prompt's details, such as object counts or specified colors. Evaluating those mistakes also requires checking whether an automated judge can recognize them. FineGRAIN combines these concerns in a structured methodology that evaluates image generators and the vision-language models used to assess their outputs.

The framework tests whether judges identify 27 particular failure modes in images produced from challenging prompts. Its dataset includes images from five generators: Flux and four SD3 or SD3.5 variants. Molmo, InternVL3, and Pixtral provide vision-language annotations, with Llama3 supplying annotations used to assess whether those models identify the relevant failure modes. This creates an evaluation of both generated content and its automated interpretation.

Analysis of the curated prompts reveals systematic problems with attribute fidelity and object representation. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that current metrics are insufficient for capturing nuanced errors. The contribution is a more targeted way to examine prompt adherence while also scrutinizing the judges on which automated evaluation depends.
neurips-2025-finegrain-evaluating-failur.tldr: FineGRAIN evaluates 27 image-generation failure modes while testing whether vision-language judges can correctly recognize them.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns from an existing dataset rather than collecting new experience during learning. Much of its sample-complexity theory studies discounted returns, where later rewards receive less weight. This paper instead addresses average reward and asks what guarantees are possible with function approximation under a less restrictive model assumption than those used in earlier work.

The authors introduce Anchored Fitted Q-Iteration, which adds an anchor mechanism to standard fitted Q-iteration. They interpret the anchor as a form of weight decay and show that it is crucial to their finite-time analysis. Under the assumption of a weakly communicating Markov decision process, they establish what they describe as the first sample-complexity results for this average-reward offline setting.

The analysis also covers data collected along a single trajectory, extending beyond independently sampled transitions. That extension again relies on anchoring. The contribution is therefore both algorithmic and theoretical: a specific modification enables guarantees about learning with finite data in a setting where prior analyses required stronger structural assumptions.
neurips-2025-finite-time-bounds-for-aver.tldr: Anchored Fitted Q-Iteration enables finite-time sample-complexity guarantees for average-reward offline learning in weakly communicating decision processes.

paragraphs: Turning a language instruction into a useful reward signal is difficult when an agent acts from visual observations. A vision-language model can judge progress, but its feedback may be noisy or poorly suited to shaping learning. GoalLadder trains reinforcement-learning agents from one instruction by discovering increasingly useful goal states throughout training.

The method asks a vision-language model to identify promising states and compare them in pairs. An ELO-based rating system combines those comparisons to rank candidate goals, reducing the damage from noisy individual judgments. The agent then learns to approach the highest-ranked goal by minimizing distance in an embedding space learned from unlabeled visual data. This converts ranked visual goals into a training objective.

The approach bypasses the need for abundant, accurate feedback to directly construct a well-shaped reward function. In classic control and robotic manipulation environments, the authors report an average final success rate of about 95%, compared with about 45% for the strongest evaluated competitor. These results support incremental goal discovery as an effective use of imperfect visual-language feedback.
neurips-2025-goalladder-incremental-goal.tldr: GoalLadder turns noisy vision-language comparisons into ranked visual goals that guide reinforcement learning from a single instruction.

paragraphs: Learning algorithms prescribe how model parameters should change, but those prescriptions are often taken as starting points. This paper asks when particular update rules can be derived as optimal decisions. It treats learning as navigation through a partially observed loss landscape, with parameter updates acting as a policy in an optimal control problem.

Different assumptions produce different familiar rules. Short-horizon optimization yields gradient descent, while longer-horizon planning yields momentum. Accounting for parameter-space geometry leads to natural gradients, and partial controllability leads to non-gradient rules. Adaptive optimizers such as Adam arise through online Bayesian inference about the landscape's shape. The framework connects each rule to the information and planning structure under which it emerges.

The authors also interpret continual-learning strategies such as resetting weights as optimal responses to task uncertainty. The contribution is a unified account of why several learning behaviors can be appropriate under particular assumptions. It offers a basis for designing adaptive algorithms by making those assumptions explicit, rather than claiming one update rule is optimal in every setting.
neurips-2025-gradient-descent-as-loss-la.tldr: The paper derives familiar learning rules as optimal loss-landscape navigation policies under different planning, geometry, information, and uncertainty assumptions.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a pretrained Transformer adapt from demonstrations without changing its parameters. This paper studies how that ability depends on nonlinear model components and mixtures of training sources. Its setting allows sources to differ in their inputs, tasks, and noise, extending theoretical treatments based on a single source or simpler linear models.

The analysis considers a two-layer MLP head whose first layer receives one gradient step and whose second layer is fully optimized. In a high-dimensional asymptotic regime, the authors prove equivalence in in-context learning error to structured polynomial predictors. This equivalence makes the model easier to analyze and shows how nonlinear MLPs improve performance, particularly on nonlinear tasks, relative to linear baselines.

The resulting analysis identifies low noise and structured covariances as properties of high-quality sources. Within the studied setting, feature learning emerges only when task covariance has sufficient structure. Experiments across activations, sizes, and distributions validate the results, while multilingual sentiment analysis illustrates their relevance to a setting where each language forms a different source.
neurips-2025-how-data-mixing-shapes-in-c.tldr: Under a specified asymptotic training model, polynomial-predictor equivalence explains how nonlinear MLPs and heterogeneous data mixtures shape in-context learning.

paragraphs: Some questions about images require knowledge that the image itself does not contain. A model must understand what it sees, retrieve relevant external information, and use that information to answer. This paper identifies two weaknesses in existing retrieval-augmented approaches: retrieval is insufficiently interactive, and retrieved material is not effectively organized for the vision-language model.

VLM-PRF addresses those weaknesses with stages for processing, retrieval, and filtering. Reinforcement learning guides the model's tool-driven information processing, allowing it to learn retrieval strategies. A separate filtering capability trains the model to transform raw retrieved material into knowledge tailored to the question. The framework therefore addresses both how information is obtained and how it is prepared for answering.

Two reward signals supervise the system so that retrieval strategy and answer generation can improve together. Experiments on two datasets demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The stated contribution is an integrated way to learn information gathering and task-specific filtering, treating retrieval as part of the model's decision process rather than a fixed preliminary step.
neurips-2025-knowledge-based-visual-ques.tldr: VLM-PRF jointly improves tool-guided retrieval and answer generation while filtering external information into question-specific knowledge.

paragraphs: Multi-view clustering groups data without labels by combining different representations of the same underlying items. Those views can reinforce one another while contributing distinct information. The paper identifies two obstacles: feature extraction can be sensitive to noise and miss cluster structure, while fusion strategies may fail to adapt as data distributions and view quality change.

LLM-DAMVC treats clustering as a dynamic decision-making problem assisted by a large language model. Each view has complementary feature-extraction agents. A contrastive module works in both the feature domain and the frequency domain to improve consistency and make clusters more distinguishable. This gives the framework two domains in which to organize useful information for grouping.

An LLM-assisted fusion mechanism supplies an adaptable strategy for learning the weights used to combine views. Its purpose is to handle complex settings and views with substantially different characteristics. The authors report extensive experiments supporting the method's effectiveness and superiority. The contribution combines improved representation learning with adaptive decisions about how much each view should influence clustering.
neurips-2025-llm-damvc-a-large-language-.tldr: LLM-DAMVC combines feature- and frequency-domain learning with LLM-assisted adaptive view fusion for unsupervised clustering.

paragraphs: Recovering an image from incomplete, noisy measurements is ambiguous because the sensing operator cannot distinguish every possible signal. Its null space captures directions that measurements cannot reveal. Reconstruction methods typically use prior information to resolve that ambiguity, but the paper argues that conventional priors often overlook the null space specific to the measurement process.

Non-Linear Projections of the Null-Space, or NPN, introduces a neural-network-based regularizer organized around a low-dimensional projection of that null space. This makes the prior specific to the sensing matrix rather than imposing constraints only on image structure. The approach can complement image-domain priors and fit into existing reconstruction frameworks, allowing measurement-specific information to inform the regularization design.

The authors provide convergence and reconstruction-accuracy guarantees when NPN is used within plug-and-play methods. Experiments report consistent reconstruction improvements across diverse sensing matrices and tasks, including deblurring, super-resolution, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging. The empirical integrations also include unrolling networks, deep image priors, and diffusion models, supporting the approach's flexibility across reconstruction methods.
neurips-2025-npn-non-linear-projections-.tldr: NPN improves image reconstruction with neural regularization tailored to the sensing operator's null-space structure.

paragraphs: Equivariant neural networks have shown empirical generalization advantages, but explaining those advantages theoretically remains difficult. This paper studies group convolutional neural networks with ReLU activations through VC dimension, a measure of a model class's capacity to represent classification patterns. The goal is to connect architectural choices with theoretical understanding of generalization.

The analysis examines how depth, the number of weights, and input dimensionality affect VC dimension. Establishing a lower bound is a central technical challenge. To address it, the authors develop techniques that reveal a connection between group convolutional networks and standard deep neural networks. They also compare their resulting bounds with known bounds for fully connected architectures.

The results extend earlier work on continuous group convolutional networks restricted to two layers. A particular focus is how capacity depends on input resolution, making the analysis relevant to understanding what changes when a network receives more detailed inputs. The contribution supplies architectural capacity bounds and new proof techniques, rather than an experimental demonstration that every group convolutional network generalizes better.
neurips-2025-on-the-vc-dimension-of-deep.tldr: The paper derives VC-dimension bounds for deep ReLU group convolutional networks, examining dependence on architecture and input resolution.

paragraphs: Understanding a 3D environment involves relationships at multiple levels of detail, including the hierarchical organization of objects and scenes. Representing those relationships within implicit scene models such as neural radiance fields is challenging. Existing explicit approaches described in the paper either require repeated rendering at different granularities or depend on predefined discrete hierarchies with limited adaptability.

OpenHype represents scene hierarchies in a continuous hyperbolic latent space. The geometry of that space supports encoding relationships across scales. Geodesic paths through the representation allow smooth movement through the hierarchy, making changes in granularity part of the learned space. This offers a way to represent nuanced hierarchical structure without restricting it to a predefined closed set of levels.

The authors report that OpenHype outperforms state-of-the-art methods on standard benchmarks, with better efficiency and adaptability in 3D scene understanding. The approach matters because it brings hierarchical organization into implicit scene representations while addressing the costs and rigidity associated with the alternatives discussed in the paper.
neurips-2025-openhype-hyperbolic-embeddi.tldr: OpenHype uses a continuous hyperbolic representation to encode and traverse 3D scene hierarchies efficiently.

paragraphs: This paper studies convex-concave minimax optimization when an algorithm can access function values but is not directly given derivatives. The objective is to find an approximate saddle point while reducing the number of function-value queries. The proposed quantum methods use estimated curvature information, represented by the Hessian, to guide optimization.

The authors construct efficient quantum Hessian estimators and build Hessian-aware algorithms around them. For dimension d and target accuracy epsilon, the stated query bound scales as d to the two-thirds power times epsilon to the minus two-thirds power, with logarithmic factors suppressed. Relative to the cited classical upper bound of d times epsilon to the minus one, this yields the reported improvement in query complexity.

A restart strategy extends the approach to strongly convex–strongly concave problems, with a speedup depending on dimension and the strong-convexity parameter. The authors also apply related ideas to non-convex optimization and reduce query complexity there. These are gains in function-oracle calls; the stated comparison is specifically about that resource.
neurips-2025-quantum-speedups-for-minima.tldr: Quantum Hessian estimation enables improved function-query bounds for minimax optimization, with extensions to strongly convex–concave and non-convex settings.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language reasoning often trains an answer generator against a fixed verifier or one trained through supervised examples. The paper argues that these arrangements can be vulnerable to reward hacking and weak generalization. Tango instead trains both the generator and verifier through reinforcement learning, alternating their updates so that they develop together.

Its verifier is a generative language model that evaluates reasoning at the process level. Crucially, training rewards depend only on whether its outcome-level verification is correct, without requiring explicit annotations of individual reasoning steps. The authors report that this verifier is more robust and generalizes better than deterministic or supervised-trained alternatives, supporting a mutually reinforcing training relationship.

Among models at the 7B/8B scale, the paper reports leading results for the generator across five competition-math benchmarks and four out-of-domain reasoning tasks. The verifier leads on ProcessBench. Both components show especially substantial improvements on the hardest mathematical reasoning problems, supporting the value of co-training verification and generation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-rl-tango-reinforcing-genera.tldr: Tango co-trains a reasoning generator and a generative verifier through reinforcement learning without explicit process-level annotations.

paragraphs: Understanding where moving objects are in three dimensions requires coordinating visual evidence, spatial sound, and time. Existing audio-visual language models and benchmarks largely emphasize static or two-dimensional scenes. SAVVY-Bench targets this gap with thousands of question–answer pairs about direction and distance in dynamic scenes containing synchronized spatial audio.

The accompanying SAVVY pipeline performs this reasoning without training. It first combines audio-visual language models with other audio-visual methods to estimate trajectories of objects relevant to the question from an egocentric perspective. It then aggregates those trajectories into a shared dynamic global map. A final coordinate transformation aligns that map with the viewpoint specified by the question before producing an answer.

This organization separates tracking objects over time from expressing their relationships in the requested frame of reference. The benchmark probes both stationary and moving objects and requires precise temporal grounding and consistent localization. Empirical evaluation reports substantial improvements for state-of-the-art audio-visual language models, supporting explicit spatial mapping as a useful aid for dynamic 3D reasoning.
neurips-2025-savvy-spatial-awareness-via.tldr: SAVVY combines visual and spatial-audio tracking into a dynamic 3D map to improve spatial question answering without training.

paragraphs: Self-knowledge distillation trains a model using information from its own outputs, avoiding the need for a separate teacher network. This paper argues that existing methods emphasize reproducing shared features without sufficiently identifying the features most useful for learning. SDPGO uses gradient information to give more weight to features that strongly influence classification performance.

The framework converts gradient information into a weighting factor that changes during training. A sequential iterative learning module combines historical predictions with current gradients to adapt knowledge transfer. It also refines mini-batch KL divergence to stabilize training while continuing to prioritize task-relevant features. Together, these components make the distillation signal responsive to the model's ongoing learning process.

Experiments cover image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. The authors report consistent improvements over recent state-of-the-art knowledge-distillation techniques across those evaluations. The contribution is a way to make self-distillation more selective: the model's own predictions provide reusable knowledge, while gradients help determine which parts deserve greater emphasis as training proceeds.
neurips-2025-sdpgo-efficient-self-distil.tldr: SDPGO uses changing gradient-based weights and historical predictions to prioritize useful features during self-distillation.

paragraphs: Delivery routes must work despite changing congestion, delays, accidents, and customer availability. Benchmarks built around static, idealized conditions may miss these sources of uncertainty. SVRPBench provides an open urban-scale routing benchmark with more than 500 instances and as many as 1,000 customers, designed to expose solvers to richer stochastic delivery conditions.

Its scenarios include time-dependent congestion, log-normal delays, probabilistic accidents, and empirically grounded delivery windows for residential and commercial customers. The generation pipeline also supports multiple depots and vehicles. These ingredients combine operational constraints with uncertain travel conditions, allowing evaluation of routing behavior under circumstances beyond the simplified assumptions emphasized by existing benchmarks.

In the reported comparisons, reinforcement-learning solvers including POMO and AM degrade by more than 20% under distributional shift, while classical and metaheuristic approaches remain robust. The released dataset and evaluation suite support reproducible study of that gap. The results identify generalization under uncertainty as a concrete challenge for learned routing methods in the benchmark's tested conditions.
neurips-2025-svrpbench-a-realistic-bench.tldr: SVRPBench tests urban vehicle routing under realistic simulated uncertainty and reveals substantial distribution-shift degradation in evaluated RL solvers.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a clothed person in 3D from one image is difficult because much of the body may be hidden and several shapes can fit the visible evidence. SyncHuman combines two generative capabilities to address this ambiguity: a multiview image model that captures fine appearance details and a native 3D model that produces structurally consistent, but coarser, shapes.

The two models are jointly fine-tuned using pixel-aligned 2D–3D synchronization attention. This encourages the generated views and 3D shapes to agree geometrically. Once they are aligned, a feature-injection mechanism transfers fine details from the multiview images onto the 3D shape. The framework therefore coordinates structure and appearance before using the image model's detail to refine the reconstruction.

Experiments report robust, photorealistic full-body reconstruction, including images with difficult poses. SyncHuman outperforms the evaluated baselines in geometric accuracy and visual fidelity. The findings support combining the complementary strengths of 2D and 3D generative models, with explicit alignment helping their outputs contribute to a coherent human mesh.
neurips-2025-synchuman-synchronizing-2d-.tldr: SyncHuman aligns 2D multiview and native 3D generators, then transfers image detail onto shapes for single-image human reconstruction.

paragraphs: Machine learning for chemistry depends on datasets that researchers can access and use without extensive cleaning or specialized preparation. The Catechol Benchmark introduces yield-prediction data focused on solvent selection, which the authors describe as particularly difficult to model theoretically. Its transient-flow experiments cover more than 1,200 process conditions.

A distinguishing feature is the ability to sample many continuous process conditions. This differs from datasets centered on discrete parameter choices and creates additional challenges for learning how yield varies across conditions. The time-series data provide a benchmark for studying those relationships, making the experimental setup itself an important part of the contribution.

The paper demonstrates benchmarking with regression algorithms, transfer learning, feature engineering, and active learning. These uses establish several ways to investigate prediction and learning from the dataset, rather than presenting only one modeling approach. The intended applications include solvent replacement and more sustainable manufacturing. The contribution is experimental data and a benchmarking foundation for those aims, without claiming that the dataset alone achieves a particular manufacturing outcome.
neurips-2025-the-catechol-benchmark-time.tldr: The Catechol Benchmark provides transient-flow yield data across over 1,200 process conditions for studying solvent selection and data-efficient learning.

paragraphs: Sparse attention speeds up language models by limiting which tokens participate in attention computations. Many methods use a fixed token budget, even though the amount of information needed can vary across inputs. Twilight addresses this mismatch by adapting the budget to the attention computation instead of holding the number of retained tokens constant.

The framework draws on the idea behind top-p, or nucleus, sampling to make adaptive pruning decisions. It is designed to augment existing sparse-attention algorithms with budget selection. This makes the amount of computation responsive to the situation, targeting the changing balance between efficiency and accuracy that fixed-budget approaches cannot directly accommodate.

Experiments in medium- and long-context settings report pruning as much as 98% of tokens with almost no accuracy loss, alongside a 1.4-fold speedup over state-of-the-art sparse-attention mechanisms. The pruning figure is a reported maximum. The findings support adaptive budget selection as a way to gain additional efficiency from sparse attention while preserving accuracy in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-twilight-adaptive-attention.tldr: Twilight adds adaptive top-p pruning to sparse attention, reporting up to 98% token pruning with nearly no accuracy loss.

paragraphs: Multimodal reasoning can be constrained when a model examines visual input once and then reasons only over that fixed interpretation. Visual Test-Time Scaling addresses this by allowing perception to repeat during inference. The model uses updated textual predictions to progressively focus on high-confidence regions across space and time.

The approach centers on an Iterative Perception mechanism, trained using reinforcement learning with spatial and temporal supervision. The authors also introduce VTTS-80K, a dataset designed to support this process. Together, these components let the model spend additional inference computation on refining what it perceives, making visual inspection an ongoing part of reasoning.

The resulting VideoChat-R1.5 model is evaluated across more than 15 benchmarks covering video conversation, video reasoning, and spatial-temporal perception. The authors report an average improvement of over 5% compared with strong baselines including Qwen2.5VL-3B and Qwen2.5VL-7B. The broader experiments support effectiveness and generalization across tasks, showing that increased perceptual computation can improve multimodal reasoning in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-videochat-r1-5-visual-test-.tldr: VideoChat-R1.5 improves multimodal reasoning by repeatedly refining visual attention during inference, guided by evolving textual predictions.
